structured_output.world_model:
Simplest model: time ≈ fixed (~0.15–0.25 s) + steps × per-step cost, where per-step cost scales roughly with pixels, plus a memory-bound large-map component (BN/GELU/pool at 31×31). Accuracy ≈ a slowly rising function of total steps/epochs (~0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, ~1.5–2.7 s/pp), with 3-seed noise ~0.1 pp (SE) and held-out 10-seed noise ~0.05–0.08 pp. Tip E027 (8.75 ep) has a held-out mean ~0.7526, below the 0.753 bar, so it sits at the margin; seeds 0–2 value 0.7547 is partly a lucky draw.

Misses explained: (1) Cutting compute that is memory-bound or in early layers (E028 freeze −0.5 s, E031 sample drop −0.6 s) saves more time than the MAC share, and the accuracy loss is only ~0.1–0.3 pp, which looks like the epoch-dial rate. (2) Averaging and regularization tweaks around Lookahead/EMA/LS (E025, E030, E032) hurt 0.3–0.7 pp: the airbench96 averaging and LS settings sit at a sharp, tuned optimum, so perturbations in either direction lose. Expect further averaging/LS tweaks to be negative or null. (3) Time is not strictly pixel-proportional; resolution changes at the early phase saved more than modelled (E026).

Supported mechanisms: early low-res is cheap (E026); the 32 px tail carries accuracy (E018, E011); the epoch dial is roughly linear; wd ×0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016); freeze/backward truncation saves ~8% time at a ~0.1–0.2 pp cost. Run-to-run: time noise ~±0.02 s; accuracy 3-seed noise ±0.15 pp; the seeds 0–2 draw changes whenever RNG use changes (the step count). Unsure: whether the freeze plus extra epochs nets positive; the winner's curse on seeds 3–12 selection; PCIe transfer.

forecasts.reason: Freeze saves ~0.5 s, +0.5 epoch costs ~0.3 s; the accuracy gain is about +0.2 pp but the freeze costs a bit, so it ends near the bar.
Math-identical systems change saves ~0.05 s if the outputs are bit-identical; accuracy is unchanged.
Probably the whitening bias already stops at 3 epochs (whiten_bias_steps=3*steps_per_epoch, 33% of steps); stopping at 20% saves little, so the gain is small.
An earlier freeze saves more time but costs more accuracy; it would likely land below the keep gate.
Diagnostic only; fresh seeds will regress toward the held-out mean of about 0.7525.
BN folding saves some memory traffic but is complex, and it carries the freeze's accuracy cost.
Diagnostic only; the profile will most likely show a large non-GEMM share on the big maps.
Replacing Muon with SGD likely loses 0.3–1 pp, since E006 gave +0.66 pp, and saves ~3% time.

cruxes: Does the freeze (E028) cost accuracy beyond the held-out noise, or is it neutral? If it is neutral, stacking it with epochs yields time gains of ~0.3 s.
Is the tip's true population mean ≥0.753 on fresh seeds (13–22)? The held-out figure of 0.7526 says no, so any further time cut needs an accuracy booster first.
Is the whitening bias already frozen early in the code (3 epochs ≈ 33% of steps)? That decides whether H2.6.3 has any lever left.
